clips.title: The receiving place waits
clips.reference_subject: pocket quantum workbench; existing empty receiving bay
clips.action: In a genuinely unoccupied view of the established receiving bay, the table lamp settles over an empty work mat and one local receiving cradle becomes ready. Keep the real gold-lattice/crystal interior and the closed main DNA access boundary readable. No person, robot, portrait performance or voice is visible or audible.
clips.camera: A slow ten-second architectural push from the receiving boundary to the prepared mat.

clips.reference_subject: inventory interface; quantum-workshop depth
clips.action: A hand holds a generic inventory display front-on. As the narrator contrasts the two sides, move far enough around its edge to reveal a paired DNA aperture behind one square, with the real staffed workshop in depth. End with both sides readable.
clips.camera: Slow lateral track from screen face to its physical edge.
clips.narration: Every video game inventory has a side the player sees and a side they never get to see.

clips.reference_subject: inventory interface; materials; equipment; repair tool
clips.action: The same hand opens the generic menu over a tray holding a gem, a shaft and a visibly damaged hand tool. The cursor passes the corresponding item, combine, equipment and repair controls as those nouns are spoken. A single selection square gives one restrained flash; the objects remain traceable.
clips.camera: Over-shoulder insert; keep menu and actual tray together.
clips.narration: The player opens a menu, selects an item, combines materials, changes equipment, or asks for a repair. A square flashes.

clips.reference_subject: inventory interface; equipment
clips.action: Show a finished tool physically placed into the player's equipment loop. Its generic slot changes from available to equipped only when the hand finishes the placement. The player takes a purposeful step forward with the tool secured. The change is completed by handling, not a materializing effect.
clips.camera: Medium-low view of hand, slot and belt; settle on the finished placement.
clips.narration: Something changes. The game carries on.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan identity; pocket quantum workbench
clips.action: At a generic inventory square, a paired DNA opening reveals the actual quantum workbench inside the pocket dimension. Move through the clear opening until Ryan, recognizable from his source face, is visible working at the table. End on his calm acknowledgment of the arriving request.
clips.camera: One deliberate push through the actual aperture into the inhabited space.
clips.narration: My world takes place on the other side of that square.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan identity; pocket quantum workbench; storage cells
clips.action: Ryan receives a closed service capsule and places it in the table's receiving cradle. As he identifies himself, his face is readable; then show the nearby occupied storage cells and his working hands. The capsule comes to a secure rest at the work position.
clips.camera: Medium portrait moving slightly down toward the receiving cradle.
clips.narration: I am the guy in the pocket. The pocket dimension is where the inventory is kept, where the work happens,

clips.reference_subject: pocket quantum workbench; staff working poses
clips.action: The assistant finishes sorting a real part into its appropriate tray while Ryan examines a request at the same persistent table. A closed incoming capsule arrives in the receiving cradle, giving the word 'inside' a physical destination. End with the assistant reaching the correct tray.
clips.camera: Track along the bench from the working assistant to the arriving capsule.
clips.narration: and where the people handling those requests actually live and operate. What looks instantaneous from the player’s side has an inside:

clips.reference_subject: pocket workbench; receiving cradle; tools
clips.action: Keep all the spoken nouns within one deep composition: the receiving cradle, the small metal coupling inside its open capsule, the assistant holding it, the tool used for a simple adjustment, and the return cradle. The assistant seats the adjusted coupling in the return carrier, completing the handoff.
clips.camera: Bench-level three-quarter view; rack focus only to each named object.
clips.narration: a receiving point, an object, a worker, a task, and a return journey. The player sees the result.

clips.reference_subject: pocket quantum workbench; physical service
clips.action: Ryan holds a small coupling under the bench lamp while the assistant tightens its existing fastener. He rotates it, checks the seated join and nods. This is one comprehensible piece of hidden work, completed before the shot settles.
clips.camera: Close working hands with Ryan's recognizable face in the upper background.
clips.narration: We get to see what happened in between.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan identity; inventory cells; quantum workshop
clips.action: Ryan stands at the quantum table with generic inventory cells visible through a local DNA transfer. He accepts a service capsule from the receiving point, checks its contents and places it at the correct work position. The visible operator gives the universal inventory claim a concrete place.
clips.camera: Wide enough to show operator, aperture and work surface together.
clips.narration: That is what I mean when I say we are the inventory space behind every video game.

clips.reference_subject: bag access; pocket workshop
clips.action: An adventurer's gloved hand opens an ordinary bag exactly matching the supplied reference. A paired DNA aperture within its existing opening reveals the much larger quantum workshop and Ryan working inside. The hand retrieves one already-present object through that opening and closes its grip around it.
clips.camera: Close on the ordinary bag, then adjust focus to the inhabited depth inside.
clips.narration: A fantasy adventurer may know it as a bag of holding.

clips.reference_subject: backpack; cargo grid; equipment slot; interface
clips.action: Arrange the source-matched backpack, a generic cargo grid display and an equipment loop within a single service station view. A hand sets the same coupling beside each access control; small helix route indicators lead toward one visible receiving point. End with the coupling sent from the selected access only.
clips.camera: Measured lateral move across the three interface forms; one real transfer.
clips.narration: Another world may present it as a backpack, a cargo grid, an equipment slot, or a technological interface.

clips.reference_subject: inventory interface; pocket doorway
clips.action: A hand reaches from the player's ordinary work surface through one small DNA opening. The same coupling is received by the assistant visible inside the pocket. Keep the outside tabletop and the inner workbench in one uninterrupted view; the hand withdraws after receipt.
clips.camera: Profile composition across the threshold, preserving both distinct environments.
clips.narration: Those are different ways to reach the same underlying system. The outside belongs to the player’s world.

clips.reference_subject: quantum workshop; working hands
clips.action: Ryan opens a received capsule at the established bench. The assistant takes its metal coupling and uses the source-matched tool to seat an existing loose fastener. Ryan performs the final rotation check and places the finished coupling in the return cradle.
clips.camera: Stable medium close-up of the complete adjustment and check.
clips.narration: The work on the other side belongs to ours.

clips.title: A small opening and a large place
clips.reference_subject: ordinary bag; main DNA access; source workshop architecture
clips.action: The ordinary source-matched bag rests at its already-open access. Through the established DNA aperture, reveal the deep, presently unoccupied receiving-bay composition inside the pocket dimension. The outside bag remains small while the inner bench light comes to rest. No new opening mechanism or zipper is created.
clips.camera: A patient low-angle depth reveal, finishing with both scales composed.

clips.reference_subject: ordinary bag; large pocket workshop
clips.action: The ordinary bag sits small in the foreground. Its established opening reveals the immense quantum workshop through the DNA aperture. A hand places one physical item through the opening into the receiving cradle, making the difference in apparent scale legible.
clips.camera: Low foreground view through the small opening into deep workshop space.
clips.narration: A small opening can lead into a much larger place.

clips.reference_subject: bag access; storage cells
clips.action: Hold the modest exterior of the bag in full view while the inner DNA aperture exposes several distant storage cells. Retrieve one item from a selected cell; preserve its identity while it passes into the hand. End with the bag's unchanged exterior and the retrieved item both visible.
clips.camera: Small arc around the bag without replacing the inside with a flat hologram.
clips.narration: The visible bag does not have to contain the physical volume of everything it can retrieve.

clips.reference_subject: storage cells; staff; quantum workbench
clips.action: The assistant opens an existing storage cell, takes out a coupling and hands it to Ryan at the bench. Ryan checks the coupling and sets it in a waiting capsule. Both the stored object and the people responsible for it are physically present.
clips.camera: Track the single object from its cell to Ryan's hand.
clips.narration: It provides access to stored things and to the people responsible for them.

clips.reference_subject: inventory cells; specialized storage
clips.action: Show a generic inventory square aligned through a local DNA aperture with a dedicated storage cell holding like-shaped crystals. Ryan deposits one matching crystal into that cell and closes the local route. The count changes after the crystal settles.
clips.camera: Tight side-on view of one slot, its route and its corresponding cell.
clips.narration: Individual inventory slots can also connect to specialized storage pockets.

clips.reference_subject: quantum workshop; linked storage destinations
clips.action: Ryan directs a received capsule from the main table toward one local DNA transfer. Through that opening, show an existing storage bay with its own recognizable geometry. The capsule arrives there while the original table remains in the foreground.
clips.camera: Wide view of the shared table and a genuinely separate destination beyond the opening.
clips.narration: The shared workshop and those storage destinations are related parts of the network;

clips.reference_subject: standard setting pages; distinct pocket destinations
clips.action: At the workshop threshold, Ryan opens one established local route onto a source-matched storage bay and another onto a differently arranged source-matched working area. Send one capsule to its selected destination, then settle with the differing architectures visible. Keep this one network, not cloned rooms.
clips.camera: Slow pan between the two distinct, framed destinations.
clips.narration: they do not all have to be one identical room.

clips.reference_subject: GERTECH relay; quantum workshop; active nodes
clips.action: Ryan seats a service capsule in the receiving cradle. The actual gold-and-blue relay nodes on the source apparatus respond in sequence, and the capsule reaches the quantum table through the paired helix. End on the delivered carrier rather than an abstract glowing network.
clips.camera: Start on a physical connector and widen to show its actual receiving endpoint.
clips.narration: The Galactic Ether Relay, or GERTECH, connects them.

clips.reference_subject: gold forge; Moon Bar supply; quantum workshop
clips.action: Through the source-matched relay opening, a worker places a small ore carrier into the network. At the receiving side Ryan accepts that same carrier at the established quantum table, opens it and checks the ore. Show supplier and recipient as two endpoints of one material journey.
clips.camera: Deep two-endpoint composition with the carrier continuously identifiable.
clips.narration: It carries requests and materials between the worlds using the service and the places supplying it.

clips.reference_subject: bag; hand; inventory square; equipment slot
clips.action: Within one source-matched service station, the hand brings the same capsule to the bag access beside a generic inventory panel and equipment loop. The selected slot highlights its actual object, and the hand sends it through the local DNA route. End on confirmed physical receipt beyond the opening.
clips.camera: Over-shoulder framing that keeps each spoken access noun visible.
clips.narration: A bag, a hand, an inventory square, or an equipment slot can be an access point.

clips.reference_subject: main DNA aperture; pocket quantum workshop
clips.action: Look through the established main paired DNA aperture as Ryan steps to the receiving table inside. A capsule crosses the threshold and comes to rest beside him. He steadies it with one hand, making the reached location and the operator unambiguous.
clips.camera: Remain outside the threshold with the true interior visible in depth.
clips.narration: The pocket dimension is the place reached through that access.

clips.reference_subject: quantum table; inspection tools
clips.action: A capsule opens on the established table. Ryan lifts its metal part, turns it under the inspection light and checks the existing fastening surface with a source-matched hand tool. He places it back on the same work mat after examination.
clips.camera: Bench-height close view with the table geometry readable throughout.
clips.narration: The quantum table is where the received object can be examined or worked on.

clips.reference_subject: main DNA aperture; actual pocket workshop
clips.action: The paired DNA strands part and form the established main aperture. Through it, reveal the real quantum workshop, Ryan and the assistant already inside and working. Hold the depth long enough to read this as access to their inhabited space.
clips.camera: A slow physical move toward the opening; settle before crossing.
clips.narration: The DNA wormhole opens the pocket dimension itself.

clips.reference_subject: main DNA aperture; inhabited workshop
clips.action: Film from the outer edge of the open main aperture. Ryan accepts a capsule while the assistant works at the actual table farther inside. The received object is placed on the work surface, giving the visible interior a completed action.
clips.camera: Deep focus across the doorway, people and table.
clips.narration: When we look through that opening, the workshop, its inhabitants, and its action are inside the dimension it has opened.

clips.reference_subject: small local DNA transfer; material receiving point
clips.action: Beside a work mat, an object-sized paired helix opens. One metal coupling passes directly into Ryan's waiting hand; he sets it on the mat and the local opening closes. The larger pocket workshop remains physically present around the transaction.
clips.camera: Macro-to-medium pullback distinguishing the small transfer from the surrounding room.
clips.narration: Smaller double-helix openings beside an item or receiving point are local transfers within that same network.

clips.reference_subject: quantum service desk; familiar capsule transaction
clips.action: Use the standard workshop service counter as a simple bank-teller comparison: customer-side ledge, clear partition and existing capsule cradle. A hand sets a document or token in an open carrier; the teller's waiting receiving cradle is visible across the service boundary. No new character face or unrelated location design is introduced.
clips.camera: A straight, readable view along the short counter and carrier route.
clips.narration: The most familiar explanation for a transaction is an old bank drive-through.

clips.reference_subject: capsule; service counter
clips.action: The customer hand places a token in the existing service capsule, closes the cap with a positive latch and releases the carrier into its guide. The teller's gloved hand receives the same capsule at the other end. End on the closed, received carrier.
clips.camera: Close enough to see token insertion, latch closure and receipt.
clips.narration: You put something into a capsule, seal it, and send it to the teller.

clips.reference_subject: capsule; service counter; receiving hands
clips.action: The receiving hand opens the capsule, checks its token at the service pad, closes it and sends the same carrier back. The customer's hand catches it in the return cradle. The people stay at their own ends of the transaction.
clips.camera: One profile view across both ledges, following the carrier.
clips.narration: The teller receives it, handles the request, and sends the capsule back.

clips.reference_subject: service counter; capsule; parked car and customer window
clips.action: Keep the customer's parked car and its open side window visible beside the same service counter; show the customer only as the established gloved hands at the window. Beyond the partition, the teller's gloved hands complete the token check and return the capsule while remaining at the counter. The capsule reaches the car window; the teller never enters the vehicle. Use an unbranded car as the literal analogy prop, with no new customer face.
clips.camera: Locked profile including car window, capsule guide and the separate teller position.
clips.narration: The teller does not have to climb into your car to do the work.

clips.reference_subject: local DNA opening; capsule; quantum table
clips.action: At the established capsule guide, replace the long travel path with one small paired DNA transfer. The closed carrier passes through and arrives on Ryan's receiving cradle inside the actual pocket workshop. Ryan opens it and shows its contents at the table.
clips.camera: Track from the near guide through the aperture to the receiving hands.
clips.narration: In our world, the wormhole takes the place of the long pneumatic tube. The service happens at the other end.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan identity; quantum table
clips.action: Ryan rests his hand on the recognizable quantum table as a closed capsule lands securely in its cradle. He opens it, lifts the small metal coupling and presents it under the table light. End with the object clearly at its working destination.
clips.camera: Medium portrait lowering into the table action.
clips.narration: My quantum table is that other end.

clips.reference_subject: persistent quantum workshop; ready receiving cradle
clips.action: The same table is visible before a request arrives. Ryan checks a source-matched tool and the assistant clears a work mat. Only then does a small DNA transfer deliver a closed capsule onto the prepared receiving cradle. The room and workers remain the same.
clips.camera: Unbroken wide view of preparation and delivery.
clips.narration: It is already there, in the pocket dimension, ready to receive a request from somewhere else.

clips.reference_subject: same workshop; second request
clips.action: A second closed capsule reaches the established table while Ryan remains at the same work position. He clears the finished work to the return tray and moves the newly received capsule onto the open mat. Show reuse of existing equipment and space.
clips.camera: Fixed bench-side view emphasizing the unaltered table and positions.
clips.narration: The arrival of a new customer does not create a new workshop.

clips.reference_subject: local aperture closing; persistent room
clips.action: A finished capsule leaves through a small local DNA opening. As that opening closes, continue observing Ryan placing his tool in its stand and the assistant preparing the next empty mat. The room, stored goods and inhabitants remain present.
clips.camera: Hold the same framing after the local transfer closes.
clips.narration: When a local transfer closes, the table and the people around it continue to exist.

clips.title: The room remains
clips.reference_subject: persistent quantum workbench; unoccupied part of the receiving bay
clips.action: Frame an unoccupied section of the same quantum receiving table after its local transfer has closed. Its stored tools, waiting cradle, light and material trays remain in place. A tethered loose tool slowly settles into its magnetic stand. Keep workers outside this composition rather than making them disappear.
clips.camera: A quiet locked-off ten-second observation of the preserved working space.

clips.reference_subject: damaged hand tool; generic repair control
clips.action: Introduce tool T1: a source-matched short-handled pick with a triangular head notch and one visibly loose retaining pin. The player's hand wiggles its loose joint and selects repair on the adjacent generic inventory control. End on the same damaged tool laid in the service carrier.
clips.camera: Close enough to identify the notch and loose pin; include the repair selection.
clips.narration: Consider a damaged tool. On the player’s side, someone selects repair.

clips.reference_subject: T1 repair tool; capsule; quantum table
clips.action: Inside the pocket workshop, the same carrier delivers T1, recognizable by its triangular notch and loose pin, to the quantum table. Ryan opens the carrier, lifts the tool and moves the loose head gently to expose the fault. End with the pin and joint clearly visible.
clips.camera: Follow the carrier onto the table, then settle on the actual break.
clips.narration: On our side, that same damaged tool arrives at the quantum table. We can see what is broken.

clips.reference_subject: T1; existing pin; source hand tool
clips.action: Ryan supports T1 on the table fixture. The assistant realigns its existing head, reseats the original retaining pin with the source-matched hand tool and tests the joint under light pressure. The head holds firmly; Ryan nods at the completed repair.
clips.camera: Stable macro view of alignment, seating and the successful test.
clips.narration: Somebody handles it, fixes the fault, and checks the result.

clips.reference_subject: same repaired T1; return aperture; inventory slot
clips.action: The original notched T1 returns through the same object-sized DNA route in its carrier. The player takes it, tests the now-solid head, then places it in its original equipment slot. Only after receipt does the generic damaged-state indicator become restored.
clips.camera: Track the single identifiable tool from the aperture to the hand and slot.
clips.narration: The same tool goes back through the appropriate opening, and the player’s inventory reflects its restored condition.

clips.reference_subject: restored T1; closed carrier; repair receipt
clips.action: Keep restored T1 in the player's hand beside the now-empty service carrier and its confirmed inventory slot. On 'in, fix, out,' show the clear receiving/return positions and the solid repair; the hand makes one final safe test and secures T1. Do not re-break or repeat its journey.
clips.camera: Calm close view resolving the completed service.
clips.narration: The essential action is simple: in, fix, out.

clips.title: A repaired tool leaves with its owner
clips.reference_subject: restored T1; source-matched adventure-side threshold
clips.action: The player checks that the restored triangular-notched T1 is secured at the belt and walks fully across the existing adventure-side threshold. Let the departure finish, then hold the vacated service position. The tool stays repaired and leaves with the same owner.
clips.camera: Medium-low follow to the real doorway; settle after the complete exit.

clips.reference_subject: repair bench; original parts; inspection fixture
clips.action: At the same workshop, Ryan checks a separately received loose coupling and seats its existing fastener with the hand tool already on the mat. The coupling's original pieces remain together; its tiny repair is completed without disassembling a whole machine or introducing a new factory.
clips.camera: Medium close view of one small repair in the persistent space.
clips.narration: A repair request stays a repair request. It does not require the entire tool to be manufactured again.

clips.reference_subject: two distinct work trays; gem; shaft; repair part
clips.action: Ryan places a repair coupling on one work mat and a real gem with its shaft on another. He returns the completed coupling to its carrier, then turns to the separate assembly request. The camera makes the distinct jobs readable without an abstract process montage.
clips.camera: Slow bench-level move from repair tray to assembly tray.
clips.narration: Other requests can involve fabrication or combining materials, but those are different jobs.

clips.reference_subject: gem; shaft; capsule; workbench
clips.action: A service carrier opens to reveal one gem and one shaft. The assistant places both actual materials on the table, checks the fitted socket and seats the gem into the shaft's existing gold collar. Ryan steadies the same shaft for the final fastening.
clips.camera: Close view of incoming materials, hands and the actual joining point.
clips.narration: If a gem and a shaft are sent for assembly, those actual materials arrive at the worker’s desk.

clips.reference_subject: assembled gem-and-shaft item; return carrier
clips.action: Ryan checks the seated gem on the same shaft, gives the existing collar its final fastening and places the completed item in the correct return carrier. The carrier closes and departs through its local DNA transfer. End on the cleared assembly mat.
clips.camera: Unbroken view of final test, packing and departure.
clips.narration: The finished item returns after the work is done.

clips.reference_subject: quantum workshop; materials; finished equipment
clips.action: Show Ryan and the established assistant physically handling supplied ore, a waiting work carrier and one finished source-matched tool on the same bench. The assistant presents the tool; Ryan checks it and sets it into the return cradle. The workforce and material source remain visible.
clips.camera: Medium-wide work scene with foreground ore and completed tool.
clips.narration: This gives ordinary game actions a place, a workforce, and a story. Equipment comes from somebody’s work. Materials arrive from somewhere.

clips.reference_subject: repair hands; silk wardrobe service
clips.action: A damaged coupling passes from the receiving cradle into Ryan's hand. Beside that work position, the same established brunette porcelain assistant lays an actual silk gown over an opaque dressing screen for a fully covered customer. End with repair and wardrobe requests physically received.
clips.camera: Track the real handoff and arrive at the adjoining silk service area.
clips.narration: Damaged objects pass through someone’s hands. The assistants who handle adventurers’ clothing are also the people behind the equipment change

clips.reference_subject: silk gown; covered wardrobe change; inventory clothing slot
clips.action: The assistant smooths a source-matched silk gown onto the already-covered adult customer while the dressing screen maintains coverage. The garment is physically fitted and the helper steps back to inspect it. Only after the fit is complete does the generic clothing slot give its brief confirmation flash.
clips.camera: Medium side view of working hands, silk drape and settled finished outfit.
clips.narration: the player usually sees as a brief flash.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan chief craftsman; coins; drops; ore; return carrier
clips.action: Ryan receives a small coin tray, a source-matched recovered drop and a real ore carrier at the quantum table. He checks them against the waiting request and hands the correctly packed result to the assistant's return cradle. Show each named material during its phrase.
clips.camera: Bench-level move across the received materials to Ryan's working face.
clips.narration: I am the chief craftsman among them: receiving the coins, drops, ore, and requests, then helping send the results back.

clips.reference_subject: vast zero-G ether; suspended quantum table; local routes
clips.action: Reveal the expansive source-matched ether workshop: Ryan and the established assistant drift slowly beside the anchored quantum table while small addressed transfers bring carriers to its receiving points. Ryan catches one carrier and secures it to the work surface. End on controlled work within the vast space.
clips.camera: Slow wide orbit with clear scale and restrained drift.
clips.narration: Some scenes reveal that world as a vast, weightless ether, with workers and transfer openings around the quantum table.

clips.reference_subject: zero-G ether; tethered tools; controlled movement
clips.action: Ryan moves hand-over-hand along the existing table edge while a tethered tool floats nearby. He arrests the tool gently and docks it in its stand. Hair and fabric drift in empty ether without water bubbles, surface caustics or swimming strokes.
clips.camera: Medium tracking view following the gentle arrest and docking.
clips.narration: Its drifting movement can resemble swimming, but the setting is zero-G ether.

clips.reference_subject: spawn receiving platform; loading interface; relay
clips.action: Through the source-matched spawn access, show the fully clothed adult customer's boots meet the existing receiving platform. Ryan's assistant steadies the arriving customer and directs them to the service position. A generic loading indicator stays on the distant outside interface; it is not a new world-spawn machine.
clips.camera: Wide threshold view including actual arrival, platform and service direction.
clips.narration: The larger system also connects to spawn points and the activity hidden by a loading screen.

clips.reference_subject: loading display; actual service beyond aperture
clips.action: A generic waiting indicator sits in the near foreground. Through the already-open DNA route beyond it, Ryan receives a capsule, checks the physical part and places the result in a return carrier. End when the result is physically received outside and the waiting indicator clears.
clips.camera: Keep the display and true working depth visible together.
clips.narration: The waiting screen is what the player sees while something is happening on the other side.

clips.reference_subject: different pocket cells; finite boundaries
clips.action: Ryan looks into a source-matched storage cell whose structured boundary and actual contents are visible. He places a single stored crystal in its proper position and closes the cell. End on the comprehensible bounded space rather than a limitless starfield.
clips.camera: Measured push toward the bounded cell, then hold its physical edge.
clips.narration: The word “pocket” does not mean that every destination contains an unlimited, fully formed universe.

clips.reference_subject: finite memory pocket; limited storage
clips.action: Ryan opens a dedicated small storage pocket, revealing a fixed arrangement of occupied positions. He deposits one matching crystal into its final available place and closes the receiving control. The limited compartment remains visibly full.
clips.camera: Close framed view of one storage destination and its last vacant position.
clips.narration: Some pockets are finite memory spaces.

clips.reference_subject: finite stack; item-class compartments; full slot
clips.action: At a full crystal compartment, Ryan compares one additional crystal with the occupied positions and places it into another available matching compartment. A different-shaped tool rests in its own separate bay. The limits are shown by geometry and handling as well as color.
clips.camera: Stable view including the full compartment, alternative position and distinct tool bay.
clips.narration: They have limits on what they can hold, how much can be stacked, and what kinds of things belong there.

clips.reference_subject: larger inhabited workshop pocket; living space
clips.action: A source-matched wider workshop pocket opens to reveal a working table, the assistant and a recognizable inhabited area beyond. Ryan enters along its actual access threshold, sets down a carrier and joins the ongoing work. The space supports more than a storage shelf.
clips.camera: Wide doorway view followed by a modest inward track.
clips.narration: Another pocket can support a workshop or a larger inhabited environment.

clips.reference_subject: storage capacity; bounded structured pocket
clips.action: Ryan works beside a large, well-stocked storage array ending at a clear source-matched lattice boundary. He retrieves a crystal, then touches the array's existing control at its finite edge. End with abundant storage and the still-visible limit both readable.
clips.camera: Lateral reveal along the stock to the edge of the structured space.
clips.narration: Capacity and completeness are separate questions: having a great deal of storage does not automatically make a place a complete universe.

clips.title: The edge of a pocket
clips.reference_subject: limited pocket; existing bounded storage lattice
clips.action: With no inhabitants in this shot, move across the source-matched storage lattice to its visible structural boundary. A small delivered carrier settles in a finite cradle inside that limit. Hold the boundary and the functional contents together; do not invent a whole universe being destroyed.
clips.camera: A gentle lateral architectural reveal ending at the coherent physical edge.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan mechanical form; limited pocket; same face
clips.action: Inside a source-matched limited pocket, reveal the mechanical Ryan already functioning at a compact work position. His real face and beard silhouette remain recognizable through the established mechanical material treatment. He seats a small work component and looks up at the incoming request.
clips.camera: Move from the working manufactured hand to his recognizable face.
clips.narration: That distinction explains the mechanical version of me.

clips.reference_subject: incomplete pocket; physically bounded lattice
clips.action: Mechanical Ryan stands within a structured pocket cell whose lattice ends visibly at its boundary. He closes a small local transfer after receiving a part and sets it on the work surface. The view keeps the bounded, incomplete extent readable without depicting a whole ruined universe.
clips.camera: Slow wide reveal of the existing structured boundary and functioning work position.
clips.narration: Some of these pockets are incomplete dimensions.

clips.reference_subject: limited pocket; mechanical Ryan; organic customer outside
clips.action: Look across a source-matched access boundary: the fully clothed organic customer remains in the outside world, while Ryan's mechanical form works inside the limited pocket. A gloved hand sends a part; mechanical Ryan receives it without the organic body entering. Show no bodily injury or invented conversion process.
clips.camera: Profile view across the actual dimensional threshold.
clips.narration: Within the rules of this world, they cannot sustain everything required for a fully organic human body.

clips.reference_subject: mechanical Ryan; compact work position
clips.action: Mechanical Ryan lifts the received part with his manufactured hand, rotates it under the existing work light and seats it in the table fixture. His source-matched likeness remains clear. End on the successful action within the pocket's limited structure.
clips.camera: Medium portrait with hands and visible mechanical construction.
clips.narration: The version of me inside has to function within what that pocket can support.

clips.reference_subject: condensed mechanical Ryan; limited pocket; outside hand
clips.action: Through the small open access, show the mechanical Ryan already at work inside the compact structured environment. The outside hand places a service carrier at the threshold and Ryan receives it. Keep both scales readable without inventing an organic-to-machine transformation.
clips.camera: Outside close view through the aperture into the coherent inner scene.
clips.narration: He is condensed into a form suited to that limited reality, and in those cases the form is mechanical.

clips.reference_subject: organic customer outside; mechanical Ryan inside
clips.action: The unaltered organic customer hand reaches from its ordinary outside setting to the receiving aperture. Mechanical Ryan accepts the service object on the other side. The customer hand withdraws unchanged, and both remain at their own work positions.
clips.camera: Hold both sides of the transfer in one profile composition.
clips.narration: The customer outside the pocket has not undergone that condensation. They are reaching into the service from their own world.

clips.reference_subject: mechanical Ryan; outside organic hand; shared object
clips.action: From within the limited pocket, mechanical Ryan checks the actual object, secures it in the return carrier and passes it to the outside organic hand. Preserve the same identity and object through the threshold, with their different body materials readable.
clips.camera: Reverse profile view of the single return transaction.
clips.narration: I am operating inside the more restricted reality. That is why the two sides can show different kinds of embodiment.

clips.reference_subject: limited pocket; stable mechanical work
clips.action: Mechanical Ryan completes a fastening at his bounded work position and docks the tool. Let the view include the particular incomplete pocket's edge rather than suggesting every environment has this form. End on one functioning local work area.
clips.camera: A calm medium-wide shot with the structural boundary in view.
clips.narration: This applies to the pockets that have those limitations.

clips.reference_subject: habitable ether garden; organic life; worker
clips.action: At the source-matched ether garden access, a healthy plant and the fully clothed organic customer's gloved hand are visible within a habitable pocket. The assistant receives a plant tray and seats it in an existing cultivated bed. Organic life remains healthy and present.
clips.camera: Wide enough to read a genuine inhabited garden space.
clips.narration: It does not mean every pocket is incapable of sustaining life, or that every inhabitant everywhere must be mechanical.

clips.reference_subject: distinct pocket boundary; suitable receiving destination
clips.action: Ryan inspects the source-matched destination before sending a carrier. He selects the appropriate receiving point, delivers the carrier there and confirms physical receipt. Show one destination's actual conditions and geometry as the basis for that choice.
clips.camera: Over-shoulder view from Ryan's face to the chosen destination.
clips.narration: The nature of the particular pocket matters.

clips.reference_subject: gear-driven Ryan; source mechanical details
clips.action: Show the already-established gear-driven Ryan adjusting one small work part. Exposed source-matched gears and linkages move as his hand tightens the fastener, then settle when the task is complete. Preserve his recognizable face; do not introduce new armor or replace him with a generic presenter.
clips.camera: Begin on functional gears and widen to the same working person.
clips.narration: Mechanical life can have more than one appearance. The gear-driven version remains part of the world.

clips.reference_subject: approved porcelain brunette; white ceramic; gold; blue mana
clips.action: Ryan stands beside the established brunette android. Her bright white glazed porcelain, fine gold inlay and living blue mana veins are clearly visible. On a small existing damaged ceramic area at her forearm, show gold beginning to branch along the fracture with the growth quality of coral or crystal.
clips.camera: Careful macro approach from her consistent face to the ceramic surface.
clips.narration: Another version uses living porcelain, gold, and blue mana. At that level of nanite technology, repair resembles coral or crystal growth.

clips.reference_subject: same porcelain forearm; dynamic gold repair
clips.action: On the same small ceramic fracture, gold emerges from within and branches across the gap. White porcelain grows over the supported opening; as the glaze closes, the gold bridge withdraws beneath the restored surface. Living blue mana remains visible inside. Finish with a smooth healed area, not a permanent gold-filled crack.
clips.camera: One stable macro view of the complete repair on the same patch.
clips.narration: The porcelain fractures, gold emerges to bridge the opening, the ceramic grows back over it, and the gold withdraws inside.

clips.reference_subject: healed porcelain assistant; same likeness; working motion
clips.action: The healed porcelain assistant flexes the repaired arm naturally, then receives a real carrier from Ryan and places it securely on the table. Keep the luminous white ceramic, fine gold details and blue mana, with her established face and hair unchanged.
clips.camera: Medium working portrait, ending on the controlled carrier placement.
clips.narration: An engineered body can be elegant, smooth, and capable of growth while still being a machine.

clips.reference_subject: ordinary pocket access; existing bag; workshop inside
clips.action: A hand reaches toward the ordinary pocket or bag opening already present in the selected source. The established DNA aperture reveals Ryan working at his bench inside. The hand pauses at the unexpected inhabited view, allowing a restrained visual double take.
clips.camera: Close outside view with the existing pocket and distant working figure visible.
clips.narration: The pocket joke grows naturally out of all this.

clips.reference_subject: existing pocket opening; Ryan inside
clips.action: Open only the pocket or bag access already depicted in the source. Through its DNA aperture, reveal the same recognizable Ryan at the actual quantum workbench. He glances up from a received carrier and acknowledges the outside hand. Do not add or redesign a zipper.
clips.camera: A gentle push toward the source's existing opening, ending on Ryan's reaction.
clips.narration: Somebody opens a pocket and discovers there really is a guy in it.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan working inside pocket; inventory service
clips.action: From inside the pocket dimension, Ryan turns back to his work, opens the waiting capsule and passes its part to the assistant's work mat. The outside opening remains visible behind him, making the pocket joke coexist with actual service.
clips.camera: Medium working view with the threshold in the background.
clips.narration: He is there doing the work behind the inventory.

clips.reference_subject: existing pocket; actual person at work inside
clips.action: Frame the ordinary pocket in the foreground and the inhabited quantum workbench within its DNA access. A real service object passes from the hand into Ryan's receiving cradle. End with the expected tiny container and unexpected working person simultaneously clear.
clips.camera: Deep-focus view holding both scales without a graphic explanation.
clips.narration: What sounded like a figure of speech becomes a place with a person inside.

clips.reference_subject: existing zipper imagery only; source pocket
clips.action: Use the exact zipper already visible in the owner-supplied pocket reference, or an unaltered insert from the owner's existing zipper footage. Keep that hardware in its original place; reveal Ryan beyond the existing opening. This shot preserves the old gag and creates no new zipper or zipper portal.
clips.camera: Restrained close view of the existing sourced gag and Ryan's understated response.
clips.narration: The zipper imagery already present belongs to that joke.

clips.reference_subject: established DNA entrance; existing pocket reference
clips.action: Keep the established paired DNA entrance plainly visible beside Ryan's work position. He accepts a capsule through it and places it on the table. The entrance follows the supplied helix geometry; no zip teeth, sliders or added zipper objects are created anywhere.
clips.camera: Medium view including physical receipt and the intact entrance design.
clips.narration: It does not define how every entrance must look, and it is not an instruction to add more zippers.

clips.reference_subject: main DNA aperture; actual interior
clips.action: The established main DNA aperture reveals the real workshop and Ryan already inside. A service carrier passes through a smaller local opening to his receiving cradle. He catches it and sets it down, keeping entrance and local transfer clearly distinct.

clips.narration: The established DNA wormhole remains the mechanism that opens the pocket dimension.

clips.reference_subject: existing zipper gag; source bag; DNA access
clips.action: Revisit only the zipper detail already present in the selected source or preserved footage. The outside hand rests beside it while Ryan returns a finished capsule through the established DNA access. End on the received carrier and the unchanged existing zipper detail; manufacture no additional zipper.

clips.narration: The existing zippers can keep their place as the gag they have become.

clips.title: The way in
clips.reference_subject: main DNA aperture; true pocket receiving interior
clips.action: An unoccupied view through the established main paired DNA aperture reveals the existing quantum receiving bay and prepared work mat inside the pocket dimension. The aperture remains the access to that actual space. A readiness light comes on at the local receiving cradle; introduce no zipper, new doorway or new narration.

clips.action: Show the previously repaired, triangular-notched T1 in the same player's hand. They test its solid head once and secure it in its original equipment position; the inventory already shows its confirmed restored state. End with the tool ready for use, without re-breaking or repeating its repair.

clips.action: A new service carrier delivers a different source-matched damaged tool T2 to Ryan's unchanged quantum table. Give T2 a clearly different head silhouette so it cannot be confused with restored T1. Ryan exposes T2's loose joint and begins the appropriate small repair; T1 remains delivered outside.

clips.action: The player closes the generic inventory interface, grips the restored T1 at their side and walks through the existing adventure-side doorway. The complete exit is visible, leaving the service access quiet. Do not add a portal or zipper to the doorway.

clips.reference_subject: Ryan identity; persistent quantum workbench; next request
clips.action: Ryan remains at the established quantum table with the assistant, checking the newly received T2. A waiting carrier rests at the receiving point. He looks toward its readiness light, then returns calmly to the work under his hands. End on the same inhabited workshop still in service.
clips.camera: Slow pullback from Ryan's recognizable face to the persistent working space.
clips.narration: I am still in the pocket, ready for the next thing that comes through.
